summary: Controlled area assessment. Descriptive metadata and report contents require the displayed information eligibility.

sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Six evening passes completed during two dry-weather field periods

**Instrumentation:** Calibrated long-wave infrared radiometer, contact thermistors, portable weather station, and survey control targets

**Study boundary:** Exterior masonry and immediately adjacent exposed ground within the assigned sector; no interior access was included.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Thermal response:** A compact central surface region reached the expected daytime peak but returned heat more slowly than the comparison surfaces after local sunset.

**Phase residual:** Corrected cooling curves retained an 18-to-26-minute lag across four of six passes. The residual did not track measured wind direction or surface shade.

**Spatial form:** The strongest response remained inside the same projected surface boundary and weakened smoothly toward the outer faces.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Unmapped void space, differing stone density, repair material, and surface-emissivity error remain sufficient explanations.

**Unresolved point:** No single modeled combination reproduced both the observed phase lag and its repeatable spatial boundary. The archive does not establish an unusual energy source or hazardous condition.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Repeatable low-amplitude thermal persistence; mechanism not assigned

**Action:** Retain passive comparison data and repeat only when independent conservation or subsurface information becomes available.

**Field restriction:** No intrusive sampling authorized under this record.
